figures.title: Approved cover
figures.generation_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: finished portrait 2:3 preprint report cover, one single beautifully art-directed image. Create a premium, restrained but spectacular scientific editorial cover for the user's fictional Glamuron research paper. This is a NEW design, not a mockup: flat full-bleed cover artwork viewed straight on, ready to print, no perspective, no book sitting on a surface. Design at high resolution.

COMPOSITION AND ART DIRECTION: deep midnight navy-black star field, with extraordinarily fine tiny white and icy-blue stars, generous quiet negative space in the upper third. The cover should feel like the best of a beautifully typeset physics monograph and a luminous cosmic field visualization. A compact, searing ivory-gold energy core centered horizontally around 63 percent down the page emits flowing dipole-like field lines. Keep the hot core controlled and detailed, a small pearlescent white center with gold corona, not a huge overexposed blob. Dozens of impossibly delicate, smooth copper-to-gold filament paths arc outward in large elegant loops and return toward the core. A few silver-gold filaments are brighter; most are subtle, layered at different apparent depths, receding beautifully into space. Broad loop structure is balanced left to right but individual paths are organically varied, not a flat stack of identical concentric ellipses. Needle-sharp linework, a few pinpoint glints on curves, exquisite separation between near and distant filaments. Several loops elegantly disappear beyond the page edges. Faint translucent emerald, cyan and violet auroral curtains trace a very shallow arch behind the upper part of the field image; subdued and ethereal. Let navy darkness remain dominant. No nebula clutter. Very subtle fine matte uncoated-paper tooth across the design, rich dark ink, luminous printed-gold feel; no painterly strokes and no crude noise.

TYPOGRAPHY IS CRITICAL. The typography is a deliberate, fully integrated editorial composition on the same seamless dark background as the image. There must be NO horizontal boundary, opaque header rectangle or visibly separate text banner. White/ivory type stays crisp and high-contrast. Top-left at about 5 percent from the left and 4 percent from the top: the small exact identifier 'CERN-PH-EP/2026-017' in refined sans serif with subtle tracking. Below, the title is large, distinguished, elegant high-contrast Roman serif capitals, expertly kerned, with this exact line arrangement:
OBSERVATION OF
THE GLAMURON
The second line is the dominant line, and both are comfortably within the print-safe margins. Title in upper 10–25 percent of the cover. Below the title, set the exact subtitle in a smaller elegant white serif, in two balanced lines:
Discovery of a Morphophononic Quasi-Particle
and the Slayton Field
Keep subtitle comfortably readable and separated from the title, ending around 33 percent down. All title/subtitle characters must be spelled exactly; preserve 'Glamuron' (G L A M U R O N) and 'Morphophononic' (M O R P H O P H O N O N I C). The visual field begins subtly behind the type and becomes intense only below the subtitle, leaving breathing room. Bottom of cover is artwork only.

FINISH: sophisticated cinematic depth, precise engraved-like glowing field geometry, disciplined typography, restrained jewel tones and a stunning golden center. Avoid: logos, institutional seals, authors, extra words, equations, axes, people, socks, crowns, rhinestones, decorative borders, watermark, frame, mockup, garish thick orange scribbles, giant lens flare, blown-out broad white patch. The only text on the cover is the identifier, title, and exact subtitle specified above.
figures.source_prompt: A full-page report cover for a particle-physics preprint. The background is deep navy blue scattered with small white and pale-blue stars, like a long-exposure photograph of a clear night sky. At dead center, a brilliant golden-white burst of light, slightly larger than a fist on a letter-size page, with soft bloom at its edges. Radiating from the burst are dozens of smooth, looping field lines in orange and gold, like magnetic field lines around a dipole drawn in glowing ink; the loops arc out to the edges of the page and curve back toward the center, overlapping gently. The light falls off toward the corners so the stars stay visible. Render as a crisp digital illustration, not a painting; no visible brush texture. Reserve a clean dark band across the top fifth of the page for text: the report identifier "CERN-PH-EP/2026-017" set small in white sans-serif at upper left, and below it the title "Observation of the Glamuron" in large white serif capitals, with the subtitle "Discovery of a Morphophononic Quasi-Particle and the Slayton Field" in smaller white serif on the next line. No institutional logo, no people, no equations, no axes.
